title: Musicians' pay, the union and getting started
summary: Gitler raises getting paid and weak union support; Hall explains the many stages of being hired.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah, again touching on what a musician has to go through beyond the actual learning the instrument and playing it and developing himself as a musician, and touching on what you said before about the instrument being an extension of yourself. You know, life doesn't end when you go off the band stand, and things have to do as with music directly or indirectly affecting, you know, your career, and the ad lib player, as you call him, has always had a lot of problems, maybe some the same as any working person, but there seem to be a set of problems that are always cropping up in this music which is held cheap by a lot of people, and so therefore they think, you know, they have got to get the guy to work for this. You know, don't pay him-pay him. There's always been this problem of, you know, getting -- getting your money when you should just be worrying about playing.
You mean like a doctor friend that wanted me to play for nothing?
Well, at least he could barter some
medical attention for it or at least employ the barter system.

But, no, I meant with, you know, the whole idea of -- of the jazz musician being forced to wise up over the years as far as publishing and, you know, job security and making people fulfill a contract. The union has never been known to really back up the jazz musician that strongly since I've been around.

Well, the jazz musician, I mean, it has many layers, many stages. Unless you're a genius, you don't -- you're in it 20 years before you can even think about earning a living, and the modern fellows are a little more on the ego side that their performance is the basis of their employment, and it isn't. It's only part of it. You have to go through many phases of being hired, you know, to get on the bandstand, all sorts of devious means of not getting on that bandstand, and many good musicians in this country that have never performed professionally because they never, well, got into it.
I don't know if I could have got into it if I was seeking it. It just came at a time for me that I was in it automatically.
